idea-plugin.name: archvow
idea-plugin.description:
Spec-driven development (SDD) for AI-assisted coding: architecture specifications, decisions and checks in your IDE.

An AI assistant writes code fast - and decides things nobody asked it to decide. ArchVow keeps your project's architecture as specifications: what each component must do, the decisions a person makes, what must never happen and the invariants that prevent it. It checks the code against them, locally and in CI, before any review.

This plugin brings the ArchVow CLI into IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and the other JetBrains IDEs: a visual workspace for your features, components, open decisions and checks, every ArchVow command as a guided form, and structured prompts for your AI assistant. The CLI stays the single source of truth: the plugin reads what it says and runs its commands - only after you confirm them.

Highlights

  • See where the project stands: the Overview shows what is done, what is open and what Check found, with the first finding in plain words and a button to its file.
  • Start in minutes: try ArchVow on a finished example first, then initialize your repository (or adopt the code already there) with a guided wizard that shows every file it will write.
  • Decide what matters: decisions, open questions, hazards and invariants per component, with the template's suggested answers ready to confirm.
  • Work with any AI assistant: copy a structured request (implement, review, find risks...) for the assistant your project approved; what the AI proposes waits for a person to keep it.
  • Edit .vow files with highlighting, errors as you type, folding, Structure view and navigation.

Get started

  1. Install the ArchVow CLI 2.1.1 in your project's Python 3.11+ environment, from your package index or a wheel: python -m pip install archvow==2.1.1. The plugin can show and run that command for you - only after Confirm and run.
  2. Not sure yet? Open the Archvow tool window and use Try it: ArchVow copies a finished example to a scratch folder, makes a change an AI often makes - a module nobody decided on, a shortcut across layers - and shows what Check catches. Nothing in your project changes.
  3. Initialize ArchVow in your repository (also from the Welcome screen): choose a template (Python app, FastAPI service, PySpark pipeline, LangGraph agent...), answer a few questions, review the files it will write, then confirm. Code already there? Choose Adopt: your modules become components where they are.
  4. Follow the First steps on the Overview: answer the foundations, add a feature, add its first component and answer its decisions, build it and run Check, commit. The card goes once the five are done.

The workspace

The Archvow tool window (left; Tools > Show Archvow) chooses; what you choose opens in one reusable editor tab.

  • Overview: First steps for a new project; Next (what to build now, with the suggested answers) and Check; under More, Doctor, Audit, Briefs, Budget / Next, Diff and AI review; the Architecture card (items done, open and done items), the Checks card (errors, warnings and the first finding: its rule in words, its file and line) and the project's Packs.
  • Features: what the product does, feature by feature or by layer. A feature's page: how far it is, the features it uses and that use it, its components by layer and what is open, with Add component, Open feature doc, Copy AI prompt, Next steps and Rename.
  • A component: its decisions, questions, safety (hazards and invariants), assumptions, rules, columns, tasks and spec - the items as cards, the answer panel beside them, opened on the first open item.
  • Commands: every ArchVow command as a guided form built from the CLI's own parser, the exact command line, and its result laid out. Commands that change the project ask you to Confirm and run.
  • AI skills: Draft from a brief, Find missing questions, Find risks, Implement, Review changes. A launch form says what the AI reads, may add and what you still decide. What the AI adds is marked To review until a person keeps it or removes it.
  • Show Archvow for This File (right-click in an editor or on its tab): the component that owns the file, with what it uses and what uses it.

The .vow language

Highlighting with one colour per depth (Settings > Editor > Color Scheme > Vow), errors and warnings as you read, folding, the Structure view, comments, and Ctrl/Cmd+click to the components, hazards and Python modules a vow refers to. ```vow blocks in Markdown are highlighted too.

Changes stay under your control

  • The plugin never edits architecture files itself: every change is an ArchVow CLI command, shown in full, that runs after Confirm and run.
  • It prepares AI instructions; it runs no AI model and sends nothing anywhere.
  • Nothing is downloaded or installed at startup.

How the plugin finds ArchVow

In this order, the first that answers --version runs the commands: the project's Python interpreter, the Python of Settings > Tools > Archvow, the folder's .venv, the archvow executable, the IDE's other Python interpreters, then archvow where pip and pipx install it (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin). On Windows, a Python in WSL works. Test in the settings shows which one answered, or what each said.

Requirements: IntelliJ-based IDEs 2024.3 or later; the ArchVow CLI 2.1.1 (contract 2.1) in Python 3.11+. Languages: English (default) and French. The same workspace exists for VS Code.
